target_customer: General contractors, subcontractors and owners managing construction drawings in the field
problem: Construction crews worked from printed blueprints that were quickly outdated. PlanGrid put current plans, markups and punch lists on iPads.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per project or user

founders.name: Tracy Young
founders.background_notes: Worked as a project engineer on a construction site where she was the only person in a meeting with current blueprints (2010).

founders.name: Ralph Gootee
previous_startups: First company sold to Autodesk (about 900M net per his YC profile)

technical_complexity.rationale: Rendering and syncing huge drawing sets offline on iPads and keeping markups consistent is nontrivial but standard mobile and cloud engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Project data and field habits create some lock in, yet the product category had low barriers and later entrants such as Fieldwire competed directly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Autodesk did not copy it; it bought PlanGrid for 875M net of cash, announced November 2018.

market_need_then: Construction projects ran on paper plans. A 2012 trade article noted PlanGrid was not the first iPad plan room app, and the iPad was newly adopted on job sites.

identity.voice_and_tone: Founder story driven, with CEO calling the origin the saddest story in Silicon Valley

branding.community_and_virality: Frequent press features on Tracy Young, such as Fast Company and BW Sessions.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in construction tech and a headline founder story, but no brand specific evidence beyond press features.

outcome_analysis: PlanGrid addressed paper blueprints on construction sites with an iPad app launched in March 2012, grew to 12,000 customers and 120,000 paid users by 2018 on about 58M to 69M of funding, and was sold to Autodesk for 875M. It succeeded through a sharp wedge and strong founder insight, while competitors like Fieldwire kept pressure on afterward.
notes: plangrid.com now redirects to an Autodesk page (not fetched). Some aggregators list Series B at 50M; primary sources say 40M. Closing date is reported as 2018-12-20 by one source and early 2019 by another; 2018-11 is the announcement. Seed money before 2015 not found. Founder list differs by source (Antoine Hersen, Kenneth Stone). No dated 2012 competitor named in sources, so list is empty. Name origin not found.
